title: Console IA + nav placement for Optimize Suggestions (beta) + empty states + onboarding tooltips
creator: Tessa Morgan
description:
## Problem
We’re adding a new **Suggestions** view (beta) to Redwood Console that surfaces batching/caching recommendations from Redwood Optimize. We need to decide:
1) Where Suggestions lives in Console navigation (IA + placement), including naming and any beta labeling.
2) What the expected empty states are (no access, no data, no suggestions, error) and the exact UX/copy patterns.
3) Onboarding tooltip flows so first-time users understand what they’re seeing (estimated savings, risk taxonomy, and why a suggestion may not appear).

This ticket focuses on navigation/IA and first-run/empty-state UX patterns. Detailed list+drawer UI is in **DES-188**.

## Goals
- Make Suggestions easy to discover for users actively doing cost optimization without cluttering global nav.
- Ensure empty states reduce Support load (clear next steps, no "dead ends").
- Onboarding should set the right expectations: **estimated** savings, beta limitations, and what “risk” means.

## Non-goals
- Designing the Suggestion list row layout or detail drawer information hierarchy (DES-188).
- One-click apply workflows (phase 2).

## IA / Nav Placement Decision
### Recommendation (ship in beta)
- Add **Optimize** as a left-nav section (if not already visible for the tenant), with the following items:
  - **Overview** (existing)
  - **Suggestions (Beta)** (new)
- Within Optimize > Suggestions, support deep links that preserve context:
  - Query params for filters (route/model/region) so CS/SE can share links.
  - A breadcrumb: Console / Optimize / Suggestions.

### Rationale
- “Suggestions” is conceptually part of **Optimize** (cost/perf automation), not Rollouts/Observability.
- Users looking for cost reduction will browse Optimize; placing Suggestions there matches intent.
- Keeps global nav stable while still being discoverable.

### Alternate placements considered (rejected)
- **Observability** > Cost: rejected; Suggestions is prescriptive (actions), not purely analytic.
- **Rollouts**: rejected; rollouts are a separate workflow and Suggestions is read-only in beta.
- Top-level **Suggestions**: rejected; too prominent for beta and creates confusion with other “recommendations” patterns.

## Entry Points (in-product)
- Optimize Overview should include a CTA card: “View Suggestions (Beta)” if feature flag enabled.
- If not enabled, show “Suggestions (Beta)” as disabled/hidden (see gating behavior below).

## Feature Flag / Gating Behavior (UX expectations)
We need consistent behavior across Hosted/Dedicated/Private:
- If tenant is **not allowlisted** (suggestions_beta OFF):
  - Hide “Suggestions” from nav entirely (default) to reduce confusion.
  - For internal users / CS/SE roles (if applicable), allow a direct link to show an access-denied state (useful for support).
- If allowlisted but user lacks permission:
  - Show nav item, but route resolves to an RBAC "no access" state with help text.

(Engineering to confirm feasibility; design intent documented here for consistent UX.)

## Empty States (must-haves)
Empty states should be visually consistent with Console patterns: title, 1–2 sentences, and a primary action when applicable.

### 1) No suggestions (eligible + sufficient data)
**Title:** No suggestions right now
**Body:** We’re not seeing safe batching or caching opportunities for the selected filters.
**Secondary hint:** Try broadening filters (All routes / All regions) or check back after traffic patterns change.
**Actions:**
- Secondary button: Clear filters
- Link: Learn how Suggestions work (docs)

### 2) Insufficient telemetry / data freshness
**Title:** Not enough data to generate suggestions
**Body:** We need recent traffic and token/latency telemetry for the selected route/model to estimate savings.
**Checklist style bullets (if space):**
- Requests observed in the last 24 hours
- Token metering enabled
- Latency metrics available
**Actions:**
- Link: Troubleshoot missing telemetry
- Optional: Contact Support (shown only for paid tiers if that’s a pattern elsewhere)

### 3) Feature enabled, but service temporarily unavailable
**Title:** Suggestions are temporarily unavailable
**Body:** We couldn’t load recommendations right now. Please retry.
**Actions:**
- Primary: Retry
- Link: Status page (if available) / “Contact Support”

### 4) RBAC / permission denied
**Title:** You don’t have access to Suggestions
**Body:** Ask a workspace admin to grant access to Optimize Suggestions.
**Actions:**
- Link: View required permissions
- Link: Contact your admin

### 5) Empty results due to filter mismatch
If filters are restrictive, we should distinguish from “No suggestions right now.”
**Title:** No suggestions match your filters
**Body:** Try selecting more routes, models, or regions.
**Actions:** Clear filters

## Onboarding Tooltip Flows
### Trigger
First time a user visits Optimize > Suggestions (per user), show a lightweight 2–3 step coachmark sequence. Must be dismissible and not block interaction.

### Proposed steps
1) **Suggestions overview (page header)**
   - “Suggestions are recommended batching/caching changes to reduce cost while meeting performance targets.”
   - Link: “How we estimate savings”

2) **Estimated savings disclosure (savings column or summary area)**
   - “Savings are estimates based on recent traffic. Your results may vary.”
   - Link: “Basis of estimate” (opens drawer section when present)

3) **Risk chip / label**
   - “Risk reflects potential impact on latency/quality and how reversible the change is.”
   - Link: “Risk levels explained”

### Dismissal + persistence
- “Got it” closes all.
- “Don’t show again” optional; otherwise do not re-show for 30 days.

## Copy / Terminology Constraints
- Use “Estimated savings” (never “Guaranteed”).
- Use “Risk level” with a short definition available via tooltip.
- Avoid jargon in nav labels (“continuous batching” stays inside detail content; nav remains “Suggestions”).

## Deliverables
- IA decision + nav spec (left nav placement, breadcrumbs, labeling).
- Empty state copy + layout guidance for 5 scenarios.
- Onboarding coachmark content + trigger rules.
- Hand-off notes to engineering (Console team) and docs (DX) so terminology stays consistent.

## Open Questions
- Do we ever show “Suggestions (Beta)” in nav when not allowlisted, but clicking leads to “Request access”? (Product leaning: no for beta; keep hidden.)
- Do we have tier-based patterns for showing “Contact Support” vs docs-only? Confirm with PM + Support.

comments: 2026-01-15 (Tessa Morgan): Kicking this off. We need a crisp nav decision by end of week so ENG-2404 can wire routes + gating without rework. Please include: (a) where it lives, (b) what happens when not allowlisted, and (c) copy for empty/insufficient telemetry.

2026-01-16 (Marissa Cole): +1 to keeping it under Optimize. Please avoid top-level nav changes for beta. Also, we should hide the nav item entirely when not allowlisted—Support can use direct links if needed.

2026-01-18 (Kenji Nakamura): Draft IA: Optimize > Suggestions (Beta). Recommending hide-if-disabled, with explicit RBAC empty state only when feature flag is on but permission missing. Sharing initial empty state copy options in Figma notes.
2026-01-19 (Dev Patel): For insufficient telemetry state, please include concrete checklist bullets and a docs link. We’re already seeing “why no suggestions?” confusion in other Optimize surfaces.

2026-01-21 (Dylan Brooks): From implementation standpoint: hiding nav item when not allowlisted is easy. Showing a disabled nav item with “Request access” is possible but adds state + analytics; I’d prefer hide for beta as suggested.

2026-01-23 (Kenji Nakamura): Updated deliverables: added a distinct empty state for “filters too narrow” vs “no suggestions right now.” Added onboarding coachmarks for savings/risk; kept to 3 steps max to reduce annoyance.

2026-02-07 (Tessa Morgan): Marking done. IA decision + empty states + onboarding flow are now incorporated into the Console Suggestions UX spec; ENG can proceed with routing and empty-state components.
